The ring's residency bookkeeping (ring_total/ring_count) models the ring as continuous, so after a FIFO flush the pre-gap samples are still advertised as resident and adjacent to the post-gap ones.
items.trigger: sensor_thread hits ICM FIFO overflow (sensor.c:933) or an SPI burst-read failure (sensor.c:666-671); both call icm42688_fifo_flush(), discarding every buffered packet (up to the 128-packet depth, plus everything dropped while the thread was stalled in stream-to-FIFO mode, ICM42688_FIFO_CONFIG_VAL 0x40). swing_capture_force_expire() clears only `armed`/`post_remaining`; ring_count stays saturated at SWING_RING_SAMPLES and ring_total keeps counting as if nothing was lost. The SPI-error path does not even call force_expire, so an in-flight capture completes straight across the gap. The next impact within ~903 ms (the max_pre reach) then builds a span whose pre-impact portion straddles the discontinuity, and swing_capture_snapshot() copies it with both staleness checks passing.
items.consequence: ml_thread receives a swing_window that splices samples from before and after a lost stretch of stream. swing_segment_extract locks onto the artificial quiet→motion step at the splice (or mis-measures the takeback), and the resulting swing_dynamics record — takeback_ms, tempo_ratio_x100, time_to_peak_ms, impact_phase_ms, peak_speed — is silently wrong. That record is persisted to the ZMS swing band by storage_write_swing() and pushed to the phone as a coaching notify; nothing marks it as suspect and no counter records it (expired_count is not bumped on the SPI-error path). Fabricated coaching data, not a drop.

items.invariant: ring_head == ring_total % SWING_RING_SAMPLES, i.e. the sample with generation g always sits at ring index g % SWING_RING_SAMPLES. This holds only while ring_total does not wrap, because 2^32 is not a multiple of SWING_RING_SAMPLES.
items.trigger: ring_total (uint32) wraps after 2^32 samples ≈ 49.7 days of continuous 1 kHz streaming. SWING_RING_SAMPLES = SWING_MAX_SAMPLES + SWING_STALENESS_MARGIN = 1024 + 256 = 1280, and 2^32 mod 1280 = 256 (not 0). ring_head advances via (ring_head + 1) % 1280 across the wrap, so after it ring_head == (ring_total + 256) % 1280 — permanently. For the first ~1.28 s after the wrap `ring_total - ring_count` underflows and every swing is dropped at -ESTALE; once ring_count saturates again the generation arithmetic is self-consistent, so both staleness checks and the newest_gen check pass while the index mapping is off by 256.
items.consequence: After ~49.7 days of uptime every snapshot silently returns a 1024-sample window taken from 256 ring positions away from the requested span (and wrapping across the live write head), i.e. spliced garbage that passes validation. swing_segment/swing_dynamics then produce and persist coaching records derived from the wrong samples with no error and no counter. The in-file comment asserts the opposite ('a wrap mid-capture only risks one spurious -ESTALE drop, which is degrade-safe'), so the hazard is not guarded anywhere.

items.invariant: armed_impact_gen must be the write-generation of the impact sample, so that desc->impact_off (copied to out->impact_idx) indexes ball contact within the span. swing_capture.h documents that out->impact_idx is set 'so swing_segment / swing_dynamics can consume it directly'.
items.trigger: sensor.c pushes a whole FIFO batch (swing_capture_ring_push(fifo_buf, packets_read), up to ICM42688_FIFO_WM_PACKETS = 64) and only then runs impact_process_icm_batch() and swing_capture_on_impact(). The impact sample can be anywhere in that batch, so ring_total - 1 is the generation of the LAST sample of the batch, up to 63 samples after the real contact. Any batch where the threshold crossing is not the final packet reproduces it.
items.consequence: out->impact_idx is up to 63 samples (63 ms @ 1 kHz) late, and the span's reserved 120-sample tail is anchored on the batch end rather than on contact, shortening the usable takeback by the same amount. Today the error is latent because ml_pipeline.c passes only g_span.gyro/accel/count/rate to swing_segment_extract, which re-derives the impact; but any consumer following the documented contract (feeding the snapshot straight to swing_dynamics_extract) gets takeback_ms, impact_phase_ms and the 80 ms wobble pre-window computed around the wrong sample.

items.invariant: The mapping generation -> ring slot must satisfy `ring_head == ring_total % SWING_RING_SAMPLES` for all time, so that `desc->gen_oldest % SWING_RING_SAMPLES` addresses the sample that generation actually occupies.
items.trigger: SWING_RING_SAMPLES == SWING_MAX_SAMPLES + SWING_STALENESS_MARGIN == 1024 + 256 == 1280 (swing_capture.h:55-65), and 2^32 mod 1280 == 256, i.e. 1280 does NOT divide 2^32. `ring_head` is advanced independently as `(ring_head + 1) % 1280` (line 115) while `ring_total` is a free-running uint32_t (line 118). After ring_total wraps 2^32 -> 0 (2^32 samples at SPOTON_SENSOR_ODR_HZ = 1000 Hz = ~49.7 days of cumulative gyro-on sampling; ring_total is only reset by swing_capture_init() at boot, never by the SLEEP/resume power path in power.c), ring_head and (ring_total % 1280) are permanently 256 slots apart.
items.consequence: Every subsequent swing_capture_snapshot() copies a 1024-sample slice that is offset 256 samples (256 ms) from the span the descriptor describes. The staleness guard does NOT catch it — the generation bookkeeping stays self-consistent mod 2^32, so both checks pass and the function fails OPEN, returning wrong sample data as valid. The impact is typically not inside the returned slice, so ml_process_swing either drops every swing (-ENODATA from swing_segment_extract) or, worse, locks onto a spurious peak and persists a wrong 32-byte swing_dynamics record to the ZMS swing band and notifies it over the BLE coaching characteristic. Coaching is permanently broken until a reboot. Additionally, for the ~1280 samples immediately after the wrap, the plain unsigned comparisons `desc->gen_oldest < oldest_resident_gen` (lines 285, 323) and `newest_gen >= ring_total` (line 293) are not wrap-safe and reject valid descriptors with spurious -ESTALE/-EINVAL. The in-code rationale that a wrap 'only risks one spurious -ESTALE drop, which is degrade-safe' is incorrect on both counts.

items.invariant: The wrap margin left between the enqueued descriptor's span and the live writer must cover the worst-case ml_thread service latency, so that the second SWING_QUEUE_SLOTS slot can actually deliver a swing.
items.trigger: `max_pre` is a constant 1024 - 1 - 120 = 903, so in steady state (ring saturated at 1280) every descriptor is built at the maximum span_count = 1024. Let T0 = ring_total at arm time (armed_impact_gen = T0 - 1) and S = samples pushed between arm and enqueue. S >= SWING_FOLLOWTHROUGH_SAMPLES = 120, and because sensor.c ticks at FIFO-batch granularity with ICM42688_FIFO_WM_PACKETS = 64 (config.h:318), S can reach 183 (119 accumulated, then a 64-packet batch). At enqueue: gen_oldest = T0 - 904, oldest_resident_gen = T0 + S - 1280, so the slack is 376 - S, i.e. only 193..256 samples = 193..256 ms at 1 kHz — not the 256 ms the header asserts. ml_thread is priority 5 and can never preempt sensor_thread at priority 2 (config.h:78-79), and Bluetooth host/controller threads preempt ml. Second swing: impact #2 is >= SPOTON_IMPACT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 500 ms after #1, so it only occupies the second queue slot when ml is *still* busy with swing #1 — a cycle that includes storage_write_swing (ZMS flash, documented as blocking on GC for tens of ms), ble_svc_send_coaching and ble_svc_rawswing_publish. Descriptor #2 then has <=193 ms of residency left.
items.consequence: Whenever ml_thread falls more than ~193 ms behind, the queued descriptor's span is lapped and swing_capture_snapshot() returns -ESTALE; ml.c drops the swing (increments dropped_count) and the player silently loses that shot's coaching notify and its ZMS swing record. The 2-slot swing_q therefore provides essentially no buffering: any descriptor that actually has to wait in the queue is the one most likely to expire. Because the whole span is always built at the 1024 maximum, there is no way to trade span length for margin at runtime.

items.invariant: A descriptor may only be enqueued when its span is a temporally CONTIGUOUS run of samples at sample_rate_hz; a gap in the sample stream must abort the armed capture.
items.trigger: The module's only integrity notion is generation contiguity, and a hardware FIFO drop preserves it: dropped samples are never pushed, so ring_total/ring_count stay perfectly consistent across the discontinuity. Gap recovery is entirely caller-driven via swing_capture_force_expire(), and sensor.c misses two reachable gap sources. (1) icm42688_fifo_overflow() is polled ONCE per sensor wake, before the drain loop (sensor.c:933); an overflow that occurs *during* the multi-iteration drain is not seen until the next wake, by which time swing_capture_tick() has already counted its 120 samples across the gap and enqueued. (2) sensor.c:665-670 — on an SPI burst-read error icm42688_read_fifo() calls icm42688_fifo_flush() and returns, and sensor_thread_fn just `break`s out of the drain loop (sensor.c:981-983) without calling swing_capture_force_expire(). Both are documented as following ZMS-GC stalls, the same stalls that produce the backlog.
items.consequence: swing_capture_tick() completes the follow-through across the discontinuity and enqueues a descriptor whose 1024-sample span splices pre-gap and post-gap samples as if they were consecutive 1 ms apart. swing_capture_snapshot() passes both staleness checks and returns 0, so the pipeline fails OPEN: swing_segment_extract / swing_dynamics_extract compute peak_speed, tempo_ratio, time_to_peak and jerk from a signal with a fabricated step discontinuity, and ml.c persists that wrong 32-byte record to the ZMS swing band and notifies it over BLE as a genuine measurement. No counter fires — stale/missed/expired/qfull all stay 0 — so the corrupt record is indistinguishable from a good one in the field.

items.invariant: A captured span must contain a contiguous, uniformly-sampled stretch of the 1 kHz sample stream. The module's only integrity guard is generation-based (gen_oldest vs ring_total - ring_count), which detects ring OVERWRITE but is blind to a stream DISCONTINUITY, because ring_head/ring_total keep advancing contiguously across lost samples and ring_count never decreases.
items.trigger: sensor.c:933-953: on ICM FIFO overflow (documented as reachable after a ZMS-GC stall) the driver calls icm42688_fifo_flush(), silently discarding every buffered sample, then calls swing_capture_force_expire(). force_expire returns immediately when !armed (the common case — overflow rarely lands inside a 120-sample follow-through) and even when armed it only clears `armed`/`post_remaining`; it never touches ring[], ring_head, ring_count or ring_total. The very next impact (allowed 500 ms later by the debounce) builds a descriptor with pre_avail up to 903 samples, i.e. gen_oldest = armed_impact_gen - 903, spanning generations written both before and after the flush. The same hole exists across suspend/resume: sensor_exit_low_power() (sensor.c:824-874) restores 1 kHz LN without flushing the FIFO, so packets captured under PWR_MGMT0=0x22 (gyro OFF, accel 50 Hz LP, FIFO_CONFIG1 still 0x07 so gyro fields are the invalid-sample sentinel) are pushed into the same ring and are indistinguishable from real 1 kHz gyro+accel samples.
items.consequence: swing_capture_snapshot() returns 0 for a window that is physically a splice of two disjoint time intervals, stamped sample_rate_hz = 1000. ml_pipeline then runs swing_segment_extract / swing_dynamics_extract over it, and every temporal feature (takeback_ms, apex_dwell_ms, time_to_peak_ms, impact_phase_ms, tempo_ratio_x100) is computed against a false time base. The resulting 32-byte swing_dynamics record and its coach_chain_id are persisted to the ZMS swing band and notified over BLE as a normal, valid coaching result — fabricated feedback with no counter incremented and no flag set (stale/missed/expired/qfull all stay zero, which is exactly the diagnostic blind spot hil_stack.c:338-377 was written to chase). The mirrored gyro-invalid case instead reliably fails segmentation, silently dropping the first swings after every wake.

items.invariant: The generation→ring-index mapping `ring_index(g) == g % SWING_RING_SAMPLES` must hold for every generation, i.e. ring_head must stay equal to ring_total % SWING_RING_SAMPLES. This holds only while ring_total is an exact count; it is destroyed by the uint32 wrap because SWING_RING_SAMPLES (1280) does not divide 2^32 (2^32 mod 1280 == 256).
items.trigger: ring_total reaches 2^32 (2^32 samples at 1 kHz ≈ 49.7 days of uninterrupted uptime without a reboot, since swing_capture_init() is called once from main.c:350 and nothing re-inits). ring_head continues from (true_total mod 1280) while ring_total restarts at 0, so from that instant ring_head == (ring_total % 1280 + 256) % 1280 forever after.
items.consequence: Every subsequent snapshot reads a window shifted 256 samples (256 ms) away from the samples the descriptor actually describes, while both staleness checks still pass — the module returns 0 and hands ml_pipeline a wrong-but-well-formed window containing no impact (or someone else's data), producing garbage coaching persisted to ZMS and pushed over BLE, permanently, with no counter incremented. The in-code comment at line 53-56 asserts the wrap costs at most 'one spurious -ESTALE drop, which is degrade-safe'; that claim is wrong — the damage is a permanent index desync, not a single drop. Reachability is low on a battery device (uptime rarely approaches 50 days), hence minor, but the documented safety rationale should not be relied on.

items.invariant: Samples in ring[] must be contiguous in time, so that a captured span never spliced across a sample-stream gap is handed to the segmenter. The module is told about the gap (force_expire on FIFO overflow) but only the armed-capture state is discarded — the ring history that will feed the NEXT capture is left as-is.
items.trigger: sensor.c:933-953: ZMS-GC (or any) stall causes an ICM FIFO overflow; the FIFO is flushed (>=128 samples, and everything lost during the stall, never reach ring_push) and swing_capture_force_expire() is called. Note it also returns immediately when !armed, which is the common case — so a gap while unarmed is not recorded at all. Any impact within the next ~903 samples (~0.9 s) arms and, 120 samples later, enqueues a descriptor whose pre-window (pre_avail up to SWING_MAX_SAMPLES-1-120 = 903) reaches back across the discontinuity.
items.consequence: swing_capture_snapshot() succeeds (the generation check only proves residency, not continuity) and swing_segment anchors the takeback in pre-gap samples. takeback_ms, tempo_ratio_x100, time_to_peak_ms and apex_dwell_ms are computed over a >=128 ms time hole, producing a wrong 32-byte swing_dynamics record that is persisted to the ZMS swing band and pushed over the BLE coaching notify with no low-confidence/degenerate flag — silent bad coaching data, exactly the failure mode the fail-closed design elsewhere avoids. A fix needs no allocation: record the gap (e.g. reset ring_count to 0, keeping ring_total monotonic) unconditionally on the overflow path so pre_avail cannot reach past it.

items.invariant: The swing scored and stored under (session_id, impact_id) must be the swing whose impact armed that capture. The descriptor carries the impact's exact position (impact_off), but the span handed to ml_thread is up to 903 ms of pre-impact history and the consumer re-derives the impact from the head of the span instead of using impact_off, so the association is not enforced anywhere.
items.trigger: Two >5 g contacts 500-650 ms apart (both pass the 500 ms debounce: a frame mishit followed by a re-hit, or a racket/ground tap before the stroke). The second contact's span [impact-903, impact+120] then fully contains the earlier contact together with its preceding quiet run and takeback rise. ml_pipeline.c:145 calls swing_segment_extract(g_span.gyro, g_span.accel, g_span.count, g_span.sample_rate_hz, &g_seg) — desc->impact_off / g_span.impact_idx are not passed — and swing_segment.c:148-151 latches the FIRST impact after a confirmed start and breaks.
items.consequence: The dynamics of the EARLIER contact (speed, face angle, tempo, quality) are extracted, then stamped with the CURRENT impact's session_id/impact_id at ml_pipeline.c:153 and written to ZMS + sent as the coaching notify. The app joins it to the wrong shot and displays another stroke's metrics as this one's; the fatigue accumulator is also fed the duplicated speed. Nothing counts or flags it — every capture-side counter stays zero.

items.invariant: "The sample with generation g sits at ring position (g mod SWING_RING_SAMPLES)" — this holds only while ring_total is the true push count. SWING_RING_SAMPLES is 1280 and 2^32 mod 1280 = 256, so 1280 does not divide the uint32 wrap point and the identity breaks permanently once ring_total wraps.
items.trigger: 2^32 samples pushed (~49.7 days of 1 kHz streaming, or longer with sleep windows) — ring_head keeps the true modulo while ring_total restarts at 0, leaving a fixed 256-slot skew. The -ESTALE guard cannot catch it: it only compares generation differences (ring_total - ring_count vs gen_oldest), which stay self-consistent after the wrap.
items.consequence: swing_capture_snapshot() returns 0 while copying a window shifted 256 samples earlier than the descriptor's span, so the impact and follow-through fall outside the snapshot. From that point until reboot every swing is either dropped at -ENODATA or scored from the wrong samples and stored/notified as valid — silent, permanent, and mis-documented at line 53 as costing at most one spurious -ESTALE drop.

items.invariant: The captured span must contain exactly one candidate swing — the impact identified by `impact_off` — so that the record persisted/notified under (session_id, impact_id) describes THAT impact.
items.trigger: Two legal impacts ~500-870 ms apart (rally exchange / quick block; the 500 ms SPOTON_IMPACT_DEBOUNCE_MS is the only spacing floor). max_pre = 1024-1-120 = 903, so the second descriptor's pre-roll is up to 903 samples = 903 ms at SPOTON_SENSOR_ODR_HZ=1000 — long enough to contain the ENTIRE previous swing (SWING_QUIET_SAMPLES=30 ms of quiet + a <=370 ms takeback + impact N-1). swing_segment_extract (swing_segment.c:138-152) scans the span from index 0 and `break`s on the FIRST confirmed (start, impact) pair, and it is never given desc->impact_off (ml_pipeline.c:145 passes only gyro/accel/count/rate), so it locks onto impact N-1.
items.consequence: ml_pipeline.c:153 then stamps the OLD swing's dynamics with the NEW descriptor's join keys: `swing_dynamics_extract(&g_seg, desc->session_id, desc->impact_id, out)`. A 32-byte swing_dynamics record is written to the ZMS swing band and pushed over the coaching notify claiming to be impact N while carrying impact N-1's takeback_ms / peak_speed / impact_phase. The app sees duplicated metrics under two impact_ids, shot N's real coaching never exists, and the fatigue accumulator (ml_fatigue_update) double-counts the same speed. Silent — no counter increments, ret is 0.

items.invariant: After a FIFO overflow discards samples, the ring must not present the pre-gap history as temporally contiguous with the post-gap history — generation index is used as a proxy for time (takeback_ms = impact_idx*1000/rate).
items.trigger: sensor.c:933-953: FIFO overflow → icm42688_fifo_flush() discards up to the full 128-packet FIFO plus the stall duration (the code itself cites a ZMS-GC stall backlog), then calls swing_capture_force_expire(). force_expire only clears `armed`/`post_remaining`; when no capture was armed it returns false at line 258 having done nothing at all. ring_count/ring_total/ring_head are untouched, so the pre-flush samples stay 'resident' with generations contiguous to the post-flush ones. The next impact within ~903 ms builds a span whose pre-roll straddles the discarded interval.
items.consequence: The 12 KB snapshot handed to swing_segment_extract contains a step discontinuity in the middle of the takeback. swing_segment either reads it as a spurious quiet→motion start / a false 5 g accel crossing, or accepts a start that is physically ~100+ ms distant from the impact. The persisted+notified swing_dynamics record then carries wrong takeback_ms, apex_dwell_ms, tempo_ratio_x100 and impact_phase_ms with no error return and no diagnostic counter — exactly the same hazard the code recognizes for the in-flight capture but not for the ring history.

items.invariant: ring_head == ring_total % SWING_RING_SAMPLES — the reader maps generation g to ring slot (g % SWING_RING_SAMPLES) and depends on that identity holding for all time.
items.trigger: ring_total wraps 2^32. SWING_RING_SAMPLES = 1280 = 2^8*5 does NOT divide 2^32 (2^32 mod 1280 = 256), so the free-running mod-1280 `ring_head` and the free-running mod-2^32 `ring_total` permanently desynchronise by 256 at the wrap. Reached after ~49.7 days of continuous 1 kHz sampling without a swing_capture_init() (init only runs from main.c:350 at boot).
items.consequence: The comment at lines 53-55 claims a wrap costs at most 'one spurious -ESTALE drop, which is degrade-safe'. It does not: after the wrap every snapshot reads slot (g % 1280) which now holds generation g-256, so the returned window is shifted 256 samples earlier. The intended impact lands at index impact_off+256, which exceeds span_count (903+256 > 1024) and falls outside the copied span, so swing_segment_extract returns -ENODATA (or worse, locks onto unrelated older motion) for EVERY swing until the device reboots. Coaching is permanently dead with no self-recovery; the -ESTALE counter does not even flag it after the first ~1280 samples.

items.invariant: The pair (ring_total, ring_count) must be read consistently; `ring_total - ring_count` must never evaluate to a value the writer never held.
items.trigger: ring_push increments ring_count BEFORE ring_total (lines 116-118). ml_thread's `ring_total - ring_count` is two separate non-atomic volatile loads with unspecified evaluation order. If sensor_thread (P2) preempts ml_thread (P5) between the two loads — or the loads straddle the ring_count++/ring_total++ pair — the reader can observe ring_count == ring_total + 1 while the ring is still filling, giving oldest_resident_gen = 0xFFFFFFFF. Window: the first SWING_RING_SAMPLES (1280) pushes after swing_capture_init(), i.e. ~1.28 s after sensor_thread comes online, before ring_count saturates.
items.consequence: Any swing captured in that startup window is dropped with a spurious -ESTALE (and the same underflow in the post-copy re-check at line 335 can discard an otherwise-valid completed copy). Lost coaching record plus a misleading stale_count that points HIL triage at ring-lap rather than at a startup read race.

items.invariant: Samples that a descriptor's span maps to must be contiguous in time at the declared sample_rate_hz — consecutive write-generations must correspond to consecutive 1 ms sample periods. The generation-based -ESTALE guard only detects ring LAP (overwrite), never a time DISCONTINUITY in the stored stream.
items.trigger: sensor.c:933-953 — an ICM FIFO overflow (documented as reachable after a ZMS-GC stall blocks sensor_thread past the ~128-packet HW FIFO depth) calls icm42688_fifo_flush(), silently discarding ~130 ms of samples that are never pushed into ring[]. swing_capture_force_expire() then clears only `armed`/`post_remaining`; ring[], ring_head, ring_count and ring_total are left intact, so the discarded samples leave no gap marker. The next impact within ~903 ms (max_pre, swing_capture.c:219) builds a descriptor whose pre-impact span straddles the hole. The same holds for the SLEEP path: sensor_enter/exit_low_power() (sensor.c:725-875) neither flushes the FIFO nor invalidates the ring, so post-resume captures can splice in samples taken minutes earlier at the 50 Hz LP accel rate with the gyro powered OFF.
items.consequence: swing_capture_snapshot() returns 0 (guard passes — nothing was overwritten) and hands ml_thread a window that swing_segment/swing_dynamics treat as uniformly sampled at desc->sample_rate_hz=1000. When the takeback start lands before the hole and the impact after it, every index-derived temporal metric (takeback_ms, tempo_ratio_x100, time_to_peak_ms, apex dwell, jerk) is wrong by the missing ~130 ms, and the bogus record is persisted to the ZMS swing band (storage_write_swing) and notified over the coaching characteristic as a normal, valid swing. Silent wrong data, not a counted drop — none of stale/missed/expired/qfull increments, so the HIL drop-cause table (hil_stack.c:375) reports a clean run.

items.invariant: The generation→ring-index mapping `index = generation % SWING_RING_SAMPLES` holds only while the monotonic generation counter is exact. It requires 2^32 to be a multiple of SWING_RING_SAMPLES; it is not (2^32 mod 1280 == 256), so the mapping breaks permanently at the uint32 wrap, not just for one capture.
items.trigger: ring_total (uint32_t) wraps 0xFFFFFFFF→0 after 2^32 pushed samples (~49.7 days of continuous 1 kHz sampling; ~6 days if the ODR is ever raised to 8 kHz as the FRF path does). ring_head keeps its true modulo-1280 phase, but generations restart at 0, so from that point on the sample with generation g physically lives at (g + 256) % 1280 while swing_capture_snapshot computes g % 1280.
items.consequence: Every subsequent snapshot copies a window shifted 256 samples (256 ms) from the intended span, and the -ESTALE comparisons (desc->gen_oldest < ring_total - ring_count) also compare across the discontinuity, so the fail-closed guard does not fire. ml_thread receives a plausible-looking window of the wrong 256 ms of motion and persists/notifies coaching computed from it — silent data corruption on a long-running device, not the single spurious -ESTALE drop the comment at lines 53-56 promises.

items.invariant: Every sample in the ring was captured at the rate stamped into the descriptor (`sample_rate_hz`), with all six axes live. The ring is rate-agnostic: `ring_push` appends whatever the FIFO delivers and `on_impact` stamps a compile-time constant rate, with nothing tying the two together.
items.trigger: System FSM enters SLEEP → power.c calls sensor_enter_low_power() (sensor.c:725), which sets PWR_MGMT0=0x22 (gyro fully OFF) and ACCEL_CONFIG0 to the 50 Hz LP value. FIFO/INT1/watermark config is untouched, so sensor_thread keeps waking on the 64-packet watermark (every ~1.28 s at 50 Hz) and keeps calling swing_capture_ring_push(fifo_buf, packets_read) at sensor.c:1025. Any knock past the impact gate (5 g, or 0.5 g in tap mode) on those LP samples reaches sensor.c:1096-1104; swing_capture_resolve_session_id() falls back to the non-zero natural-play session id, so swing_capture_on_impact(cap_sid, cap_iid, SPOTON_SENSOR_ODR_HZ) arms with rate_hz=1000 over samples actually taken 20 ms apart with gyro registers powered down. The same mislabelling covers the 1.28 s after wake (sensor_exit_low_power), during which the ring still holds up to SWING_RING_SAMPLES LP samples that a fresh span reaches back into.
items.consequence: A racket knocked in the bag while the device sleeps produces a full swing_dynamics record built from 50 Hz, gyro-dead samples labelled 1000 Hz: takeback_ms / time_to_peak_ms / impact_phase_ms / tempo_ratio are 20x wrong, peak_speed and wobble are computed from the gyro-OFF sentinel, and the record is persisted to the ZMS swing band and pushed over the Coaching notify as a real shot (it also burns an impact_id). The device reports fabricated coaching for an event that was not a swing.

items.invariant: Consecutive generations in the ring are consecutive in time (1 ms apart at 1 kHz), so a span of N generations is N ms of continuous motion. After a dropped-sample event the ring splices non-adjacent samples with no marker, and the recovery hook does not invalidate them.
items.trigger: ICM FIFO overflow (sensor.c:933-953: overflow → icm42688_fifo_flush() discards up to 128 unread packets → swing_capture_force_expire()). force_expire only clears `armed`/`post_remaining`; ring[], ring_head, ring_count and ring_total are left untouched, so generation g and g+1 now straddge a >=128 ms hole. The next impact within SWING_RING_SAMPLES samples (1.28 s) arms a capture whose 903-sample pre-window reaches across the splice. The same hazard exists across the LN<->LP transition. Overflow is reachable exactly when it hurts: the sensor thread blocks in storage_write_shot on ZMS GC right after an impact, so an overflow-then-impact pair inside 1.28 s is the realistic case (a mishit followed by a quick second contact).
items.consequence: swing_segment scans a span in which pre-gap and post-gap motion sit adjacent, so it can lock onto a start/impact pair that never happened contiguously, and every sample-count-derived feature (takeback_ms, time_to_peak_ms, tempo_ratio_x100, jerk_norm) is computed over a window that is missing >=128 ms of real time. The resulting bogus 32-byte record is written to ZMS and notified as valid coaching; nothing counts it, so the corruption is invisible in the diagnostics.

items.invariant: The captured span must contain exactly one swing, so that the segmenter's 'first start+impact pair wins' contract selects THIS impact. The pre-window is unconditionally maximal and is never bounded by the previous impact's generation.
items.trigger: max_pre = SWING_MAX_SAMPLES - 1 - SWING_FOLLOWTHROUGH_SAMPLES = 903, i.e. the span always reaches ~903 ms before the impact, while SPOTON_IMPACT_DEBOUNCE_MS (config.h:18) explicitly ALLOWS a second impact 500 ms after the first. For two contacts 500-900 ms apart (net volley exchange, double frame contact, or tap-mode data collection at the 0.5 g gate), impact N's samples — including its own start, when its takeback is shorter than the remaining ~300-400 ms of span — lie inside impact N+1's span. swing_segment_extract() (swing_segment.h:131-143) returns the FIRST start-followed-by-impact pair it finds and truncates head-first only when the span exceeds SWING_MAX_SAMPLES, which this span never does.
items.consequence: The coaching record for shot N+1 is computed from shot N's samples but stamped with desc->session_id/impact_id of N+1: the app joins a duplicate of the previous swing's features to the new shot, and the real N+1 swing is never analysed. Also feeds the fatigue accumulator (ml_pipeline.c:165) with a duplicated speed, biasing the cross-shot decline evidence.

items.invariant: A descriptor accepted into swing_q must still be snapshot-able when ml_thread gets to it — the queue depth and the ring's wrap margin must be consistent. They are not: the margin covers ~0.2 s while the queue is allowed to hold a descriptor across a full ml service cycle.
items.trigger: In steady state the span is [impact_gen-903, impact_gen+120] and ring_total at enqueue is impact_gen+1+post_pushed with post_pushed in [120, 183] (batches are <= ICM42688_FIFO_WM_PACKETS = 64, so the follow-through overshoots). gen_oldest is overwritten once ring_total reaches gen_oldest + SWING_RING_SAMPLES = impact_gen + 377, leaving only 377 - (1+post_pushed) = 193..256 samples, i.e. 193-256 ms at 1 kHz, from enqueue to expiry. SWING_QUEUE_SLOTS is 2, and ml_thread only snapshots after finishing the previous swing, whose tail includes storage_write_swing → ZMS GC (documented as a tens-of-ms-plus blocking write in ml.c:9-13 and sensor.c:1057-1061) plus the BLE notify and raw-window publish. Any ml cycle whose remaining work exceeds that ~200 ms window while a second descriptor sits queued expires it.
items.consequence: The queued swing is silently dropped at -ESTALE (stale_count++ / ml dropped_count++): the player gets no coaching notify and no ZMS swing record for that shot, and the loss clusters exactly on the flash-GC events that also stall the sensor path, so a rally can lose several consecutive swings. The second queue slot is effectively unusable whenever ml's per-swing work exceeds the margin — it accepts descriptors it cannot honour instead of dropping them at enqueue where qfull_drop_count would name the cause.

items.invariant: The post-copy staleness check must be synchronized and ordered after every ring read so a span overwritten during the copy can never be accepted.
items.trigger: ml_thread begins copying after queue or storage delay has consumed most of the staleness margin, then the higher-priority sensor_thread preempts it and pushes enough samples to overwrite the descriptor's oldest slots. The reader and writer access ring data and generation state without atomics, a lock, or another C memory-model synchronization primitive.
items.consequence: volatile neither establishes a happens-before relationship nor orders the ordinary ring loads relative to the generation reload. The copy therefore has a C data race, and compiler reordering can render the post-check ineffective, allowing a torn window containing samples from different generations to be processed and persisted as valid coaching data.

items.invariant: armed_impact_gen must identify the FIFO sample that actually crossed the impact threshold.
items.trigger: The production caller pushes an entire FIFO batch of up to 64 samples before impact_process_icm_batch scans it, and that scanner returns only a boolean. If the threshold crossing occurs before the final packet, swing_capture_on_impact still records ring_total - 1, which is the batch's last sample.
items.consequence: The recorded impact position is late by up to 63 ms. For a capacity-sized window this removes the same amount of pre-impact history, so takebacks near the supported maximum duration can lose their quiet/onset region and be dropped with -ENODATA or produce biased temporal dynamics.

items.invariant: A stored generation must map to the physical slot containing that generation across every supported ring_total value, including its documented uint32_t wrap.
items.trigger: After 2^32 samples have been pushed, ring_total wraps to zero. SWING_RING_SAMPLES is 1280 and 2^32 modulo 1280 is 256, so the physical ring_head is slot 256 when the wrapped generation is zero, while the snapshot mapping selects slot zero.
items.consequence: After approximately 49.7 cumulative days at 1 kHz, snapshots initially fail the non-wrap-safe staleness comparisons and then permanently read samples displaced by 256 slots. Swings are consequently dropped or processed from unrelated IMU data until reboot; the documented claim that wrap can cause only one spurious -ESTALE is false.

items.invariant: armed_impact_gen must identify the actual threshold-crossing sample, so the capture retains the promised 903 pre-impact samples.
items.trigger: An impact occurs before the final packet of a FIFO batch. The caller pushes the entire batch before impact_process_icm_batch() scans it, and that scanner returns only a boolean, so this function records the batch's last sample as the impact. Production batches contain up to 64 packets.
items.consequence: The capture loses up to 63 ms of valid pre-impact motion and substitutes extra post-impact data. Swings whose takeback or required quiet-to-motion boundary lies in that lost interval are rejected by segmentation or produce truncated dynamics and coaching.

items.invariant: A generation value must continue mapping to its physical ring slot for the full device uptime.
items.trigger: ring_total wraps after 2^32 pushes, approximately 49.7 days of continuous 1 kHz sampling. SWING_RING_SAMPLES is 1280, which does not divide 2^32; therefore wrapped generation zero is physically at slot 256, not slot zero. The unsigned staleness comparisons also cease to describe chronological order across this wrap.
items.consequence: Immediately around the wrap, valid swings are rejected as stale. Thereafter snapshots read data displaced by 256 samples, generally omitting the real impact and causing persistent coaching drops or corrupted windows until reboot.

items.invariant: Samples retained as one capture span must belong to a contiguous, constant-rate stream.
items.trigger: The sensor caller detects a FIFO overflow, flushes the hardware FIFO, and calls swing_capture_force_expire(). This function disarms an active capture but leaves ring_count, ring_total, and all pre-gap samples valid. An impact within roughly the next second can therefore select a span crossing the lost-sample gap.
items.consequence: Segmentation treats pre-overflow and post-overflow samples as adjacent 1 kHz data. It can pair a pre-gap swing start or quiet run with a post-gap impact, producing incorrect dynamics, or reject and lose the first swing after recovery.

items.invariant: A descriptor for the current impact must produce a span in which downstream segmentation selects that impact, not an earlier resident impact.
items.trigger: Two accepted impacts occur roughly 500–900 ms apart, which is permitted by the 500 ms detector debounce, and the previous swing's takeback and impact remain inside the second descriptor's up-to-903-sample pre-impact span. ml_process_swing() passes the entire span to swing_segment_extract(), which scans from the beginning and commits the first start/impact pair without using desc->impact_off.
items.consequence: The previous swing is processed a second time but persisted and notified under the new session/impact identifiers, while the current swing is never analyzed.

items.invariant: The generation-to-ring-index mapping must remain consistent for the entire device uptime, including after ring_total wraps.
items.trigger: After 2^32 samples have been pushed, about 49.7 cumulative days at 1 kHz, ring_total wraps to zero. SWING_RING_SAMPLES is 1280 and 2^32 modulo 1280 is 256, so the physical ring head is index 256 while wrapped generation zero is mapped to index zero.
items.consequence: Descriptors initially fail the wrap-unsafe range checks; after ring_total reaches 1280 again, snapshots succeed but read samples shifted by 256 ring slots. Swing windows and coaching records remain corrupted until reboot.

items.invariant: Samples presented as a contiguous fixed-rate swing span must not cross a FIFO loss or flush boundary.
items.trigger: A FIFO overflow occurs during pre-impact motion before the capture is armed. sensor_thread calls swing_capture_force_expire(), but because armed is false the function returns without invalidating the ring; samples read after the FIFO flush are appended directly after pre-overflow samples.
items.consequence: The next capture can treat a gap containing lost samples as contiguous 1 kHz data, corrupting takeback duration, integration-derived dynamics, segmentation, and the coaching record stored or sent for that impact.

items.invariant: armed_impact_gen and impact_off must identify the actual threshold-crossing sample.
items.trigger: sensor_thread pushes an entire FIFO batch of up to 64 samples before scanning it for impact. If the crossing occurs anywhere except the final sample, swing_capture_on_impact() still records ring_total - 1, the batch's final sample, as the impact.
items.consequence: The captured pre-impact history is shortened by up to 63 ms and the advertised impact offset is wrong. Long takebacks whose onset lies in the discarded portion can fail segmentation and be dropped.

items.invariant: A sample generation must map to the same ring slot before and after the generation counter wraps.
items.trigger: The device accumulates 2^32 samples, approximately 49.7 days of active 1 kHz sampling, and subsequently processes another swing.
items.consequence: Because 2^32 modulo the 1280-sample ring is 256, every post-wrap generation maps 256 slots away from its actual data. After an initial interval of false stale drops, snapshots can pass validation while copying a window that ends before the real impact, causing persistent coaching drops or dynamics computed from unrelated samples until reboot.

items.invariant: armed_impact_gen must identify the FIFO sample that crossed the impact threshold.
items.trigger: An impact occurs anywhere except the final sample of a production FIFO batch. The caller pushes the entire batch before detection, and impact_process_icm_batch reports only that an impact occurred, without returning its sample offset.
items.consequence: The impact is recorded up to 63 samples late for a 64-packet batch. At full window size this discards the same amount of available pre-impact history, so long valid swings can lose their takeback onset or required quiet run, producing dropped swings or shortened and incorrect timing metrics.

items.invariant: The live oldest-resident generation must be calculated from a coherent pair of ring_total and ring_count values.
items.trigger: Before ring_count saturates, sensor_thread preempts ml_thread between the two volatile loads in `ring_total - ring_count` and pushes a FIFO batch before the second load occurs.
items.consequence: The mixed old/new values can underflow or produce a falsely advanced oldest generation, causing a valid early-boot swing to be rejected as stale and lost.

items.invariant: A generation must always map to the ring slot containing that generation, including after the generation counter wraps.
items.trigger: The device remains up for 2^32 samples, approximately 49.7 days at 1 kHz, and then captures another swing.
items.consequence: After ring_total wraps, every generation-to-index mapping is displaced by 256 slots because 2^32 is not divisible by the 1280-sample ring size. Captures then omit the actual impact or copy unrelated samples, causing persistent coaching loss or corrupted results until reboot.

items.invariant: An armed capture must be discarded whenever the hardware FIFO is flushed and the sample stream becomes discontinuous.
items.trigger: icm42688_read_fifo() fails during an armed capture. That production caller flushes the FIFO internally and sensor_thread merely breaks out of its drain loop without calling swing_capture_force_expire(); a later successful batch reaches swing_capture_tick().
items.consequence: Samples lost by the flush are invisible to ring_total, so pre-gap and post-gap data are stitched together and accepted as a continuous swing. The device can persist and transmit corrupted coaching instead of dropping the damaged capture.

items.invariant: Every sample in a captured span must have the sample rate and enabled axes recorded in swing_window.sample_rate_hz.
items.trigger: The production power path changes the IMU from 1 kHz gyro+accel to 50 Hz accel-only during SLEEP, while sensor_thread continues feeding FIFO packets into this ring; a capture is then armed with rate_hz=1000 before enough full-rate samples have replaced the low-power history.
items.consequence: The window mixes 50 Hz gyro-off data with 1 kHz data but is labeled entirely as 1 kHz. Segmentation can fail to find takeback motion, and any accepted timing, tempo, dwell, and integration-derived metrics are incorrect.

items.invariant: The ml_thread reader must observe a coherent generation state and must not race with writes to ring slots it is copying.
items.trigger: The higher-priority sensor_thread preempts ml_thread between the separate ring_total and ring_count loads, or advances far enough to overwrite gen_oldest while ml_thread is inside the copy loop.
items.consequence: volatile does not provide an atomic snapshot or synchronize the plain ring accesses. The reader can compute an impossible oldest generation and drop a valid capture; if a referenced slot is overwritten during copying, the conflicting non-atomic accesses constitute a C data race, so the post-copy check cannot reliably guarantee that torn samples are rejected.

items.invariant: armed_impact_gen must identify the FIFO packet that actually crossed the impact threshold.
items.trigger: An impact occurs before the final packet of a production FIFO burst. sensor_thread pushes the entire burst, then scans it for impact, and this function unconditionally chooses ring_total - 1.
items.consequence: The nominal impact is shifted by up to 63 ms to the burst tail. Although the downstream segmenter rescans for contact, the fixed 1024-sample capture consequently loses up to 63 ms of oldest pre-impact history, causing sufficiently long or slow swings to lose their takeback start and be dropped or truncated.

items.invariant: After a FIFO discontinuity, no future descriptor may treat pre-gap and post-gap samples as one continuous 1 kHz stream.
items.trigger: The sensor FIFO overflows and is flushed. sensor_thread calls swing_capture_force_expire(), then another impact occurs before at least SWING_MAX_SAMPLES of fresh samples have replaced the old ring contents.
items.consequence: The next capture can combine samples from opposite sides of the data-loss gap. Segmentation may select the previous swing or compute dynamics across a fictitious continuous interval, persisting and notifying corrupted coaching data under the new impact ID.

items.invariant: A generation must always map to the ring slot containing that generation's sample.
items.trigger: Continuous sampling pushes 2^32 samples, approximately 49.7 active days at 1 kHz, causing the uint32_t ring_total generation to wrap.

items.invariant: The reader must either obtain an untorn ring span or reliably reject it when the producer overwrites that span during copying.

Volatile generation counters neither synchronize ring accesses nor provide a compiler barrier around the copy, so the post-check cannot guarantee that optimized ring loads remain bracketed by it; a torn window can be accepted and persisted or transmitted.

items.invariant: armed_impact_gen must identify the FIFO packet that actually crossed the impact threshold.

items.invariant: A generation must map to the ring slot where that generation was written for the device's full supported uptime.

For a 64-packet batch whose threshold crossing occurs at index i, the real impact generation is ring_total - 64 + i, while this code records ring_total - 1.
items.consequence: The capture is shifted by up to 63 ms: it loses the same amount of pre-impact takeback and retains excess post-impact data. Long takebacks can be truncated, causing valid swings to be dropped as -ENODATA or producing shortened and incorrect timing metrics.

items.invariant: The reader's staleness decision and ring copy must be synchronized with the producer; a volatile qualifier does not make concurrent C accesses atomic or establish a happens-before relationship.
items.trigger: The priority-2 sensor thread preempts the priority-5 ml thread while swing_capture_snapshot reads ring_total, ring_count, or ring elements and swing_capture_ring_push writes them. No lock, atomic operation, sequence counter, or other synchronization protects these conflicting accesses.
items.consequence: The program has data races under the C memory model. Compiler reordering or inconsistent counter observations can defeat the intended post-copy guard, return a torn window as valid, or spuriously discard a valid swing.

items.invariant: After a FIFO gap, no later capture may treat samples from opposite sides of that gap as a contiguous 1 kHz stream.

This function only disarms an active post-impact capture; it leaves ring_head, ring_count, and ring_total unchanged. If overflow occurs during takeback while armed is false, it changes no capture state at all.
items.consequence: The next impact can snapshot pre-overflow and post-overflow samples as adjacent samples. Segmentation and timing metrics then operate on a silently discontinuous window, producing corrupted coaching or accepting a swing that should have been dropped.

Volatile generation counters neither synchronize those accesses nor prevent the compiler from moving ordinary ring reads across the checks, so the function can exhibit undefined behavior or accept a torn window, producing corrupted coaching and persisted swing data instead of failing closed.

items.invariant: A generation must always map to the ring slot where that generation was written, including across ring_total rollover.

Subsequent snapshots map generations 256 slots away from their actual locations, generally omitting the real impact and dropping every coaching capture or processing unrelated samples until reboot; rollover also temporarily truncates pre-impact history because the wrapped generation is treated as the total number of prior samples.
